title and abstract.summary: This study assessed the morphological traits of beetles and ants across four different biotopes in Table Mountain National Park to evaluate how the functional trait composition of these insect groups responds to passive restoration following the removal of invasive pine.

results.summary: The study measured functional richness, functional dispersion, and RaoQ for predatory and herbivorous beetle species, as well as functional dispersion, RaoQ, functional richness, and functional diversity for all ant species (including ground-nesting and opportunistic species) across different biotopes (pine, new recovering fynbos, and old recovering fynbos).
